name: Carni
description: Carni is a rubber-guard shoulder-lock configuration in which the bottom player clears a leg around the head, clamps the shoulder, and controls the arm while turning partly belly down.
summary: Carni is a rubber-guard shoulder-lock configuration in which the bottom player clears a leg around the head, clamps the shoulder, and controls the arm while turning partly belly down.
overview:
The guard player has a high leg and an overhook-side shoulder connection. The controlling leg has cleared around the head while the knee stays close to the torso. The guard player turns partly belly down and anchors the foot to limit posture recovery. Triceps and wrist control isolate the captured arm for a controlled shoulder-lock threat.

Richie Martinez demonstrates the configuration from Z guard through Jersey. The legs help anchor the upper body, but the submission target is the shoulder; a calf slicer, heel hook, or kneebar requires a separate lower-body capture. Terminology: Carnie, Carni shoulder-lock control.

Use the guard and shoulder connection to bring the opponent close before moving the high leg. Manage the shoulder and neck line with a forearm frame as the leg clears the head. Turn partly belly down with the knee close and foot supported rather than wrenching the leg across the head.

Shoulder pressure can arrive before a large movement is visible. Stop at control during drills, tap early, and never combine a fixed wrist with an explosive roll or a forced stack.

Instructional sources: [Richie Martinez — Carni shoulder lock from Z guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iClQ2Np-n30).
key_principles: Set the upper-body angle: Use the guard and shoulder connection to bring the opponent close before moving the high leg.
Frame before clearing: Manage the shoulder and neck line with a forearm frame as the leg clears the head.
Anchor through the hips: Turn partly belly down with the knee close and foot supported rather than wrenching the leg across the head.
Hold the triceps: Keep the captured arm connected so the opponent cannot freely roll or withdraw the shoulder.
Control before finishing: Hold the wrist and elbow at a comfortable angle; a small change can load the shoulder rapidly.
Let the lock go: Release the wrist and leg clamp immediately on a tap or when the partner needs to roll safely.

top.name: Carni Top
top.description: Carni top perspective: A leg clearing the head with an overhook is an upper-body trap, even if a butterfly hook remains below. Avoid reaching away while the opponent sets the triceps control.
top.overview:
The top player is responsible for recognizing and defending the control. The guard player has a high leg and an overhook-side shoulder connection. The controlling leg has cleared around the head while the knee stays close to the torso. The guard player turns partly belly down and anchors the foot to limit posture recovery. Triceps and wrist control isolate the captured arm for a controlled shoulder-lock threat.

A leg clearing the head with an overhook is an upper-body trap, even if a butterfly hook remains below. Avoid reaching away while the opponent sets the triceps control. Maintain a balanced base and a safe inside frame before the shoulder becomes clamped.

Create slack around the shoulder and elbow before moving the hips past the legs. Do not force a forward roll when the triceps and wrist are fixed; tap if pressure has already engaged. Raise the head and chest only after the arm and head-side leg are clear.

flashcards.question: Carni defense: what does a high leg clearing your head beside an overhook threaten?
flashcards.answer: A leg clearing the head with an overhook is an upper-body trap, even if a butterfly hook remains below.
flashcards.answer_line: A clamp on your shoulder and upper arm

plausible: A closed leg triangle enclosing both of your shoulders
A shin across the throat with the shoulder left free
trap: A straight-elbow lever across the center of their hips

flashcards.question: Carni defense: before triceps control is set, which arm habit limits the attacker's lever?
flashcards.answer: Avoid reaching away while the opponent sets the triceps control.
flashcards.answer_line: Keep the elbow close rather than reaching away

plausible: Reach the captured arm behind their hips
Straighten the elbow to push their far knee
trap: Post that hand wide beyond their shoulder

flashcards.question: Carni defense: how can you deny the turn before the shoulder clamp is secure?
flashcards.answer: Maintain a balanced base and a safe inside frame before the shoulder becomes clamped.
flashcards.answer_line: Maintain base and an inside frame

plausible: Lean all your weight over the captured arm
Turn your back while leaving the wrist caught
trap: Pull your shoulder up through their high leg

flashcards.question: Carni defense: what should you obtain before moving your hips past the guard?
flashcards.answer: Create slack around the shoulder and elbow before moving the hips past the legs.
flashcards.answer_line: Slack around the captured shoulder and elbow

plausible: A free lower ankle while the upper arm stays pinned
A higher chest while the wrist remains fixed
trap: A grip on the far knee without releasing your arm

flashcards.question: Carni defense: why is a forward roll unsafe when both wrist and triceps are fixed?
flashcards.answer: Do not force a forward roll when the triceps and wrist are fixed; tap if pressure has already engaged.
flashcards.answer_line: Your body can rotate against an immobilized shoulder

plausible: The captured upper arm follows the torso through the turn
The triceps grip slides toward the wrist as the torso turns
trap: The head-side leg lifts away as your weight moves forward

flashcards.question: Carni defense: when can you rebuild head and chest posture?
flashcards.answer: Raise the head and chest only after the arm and head-side leg are clear.
flashcards.answer_line: After the arm and head-side leg are clear

plausible: Once your free knee reaches the mat
While the wrist remains held behind the elbow
trap: As soon as the attacker turns belly down

flashcards.question: Carni defense: which early connection lets the guard player bring your shoulder into the attack?
flashcards.answer: The guard player has a high leg and an overhook-side shoulder connection.
flashcards.answer_line: An overhook with a high guard leg

plausible: An underhook lifting your arm while the high leg stays outside the shoulder
A wrist pull with the elbow still free to return between the bodies
trap: A head pull with both of your shoulders outside the high leg

flashcards.question: Carni defense: why does a remaining butterfly hook not make this a leg-lock attack?
flashcards.answer: Richie Martinez demonstrates the configuration from Z guard through Jersey. The legs help anchor the upper body, but the submission target is the shoulder; a calf slicer, heel hook, or kneebar requires a separate lower-body capture.
flashcards.answer_line: The restrained wrist and triceps isolate the shoulder

plausible: The butterfly hook is the fulcrum behind the trapped knee
The upper-body grips mainly prevent the heel from turning
trap: Clearing the lower hook removes the primary joint restraint

flashcards.question: Carni attack: what should your guard and shoulder connection do before the high leg moves?
flashcards.answer: Use the guard and shoulder connection to bring the opponent close before moving the high leg.
flashcards.answer_line: Bring the opponent's upper body close

plausible: Push their shoulders beyond your leg's reach
Let the overhook go while you lift the foot
trap: Straighten your leg against their distant head

flashcards.question: Carni attack: what helps manage the head-side space as your leg clears?
flashcards.answer: Manage the shoulder and neck line with a forearm frame as the leg clears the head.
flashcards.answer_line: A forearm frame along the shoulder and neck line

plausible: Both hands pulling the ankle while the shoulder-side space collapses
A palm pushing the face with the framing elbow flared away
trap: A straight arm pushing the chest while the opponent closes the head-side gap

flashcards.question: Carni attack: how do you anchor after the leg clears the head?
flashcards.answer: Turn partly belly down with the knee close and foot supported rather than wrenching the leg across the head.
flashcards.answer_line: Turn partly belly down; keep knee close and foot supported

plausible: Stay flat and haul the foot across a fixed knee
Lift the knee away while leaving the foot behind
trap: Extend the leg and pull only with the overhook

flashcards.question: Carni attack: where does your hand close to stop the isolated elbow sliding away?
flashcards.answer: Use the triceps grip to keep the isolated upper arm connected while establishing the shoulder clamp. The opponent must not freely withdraw or roll that arm.
flashcards.answer_line: Around the back of their upper arm

plausible: Around the wrist while leaving the elbow free to slide back
Across the front of the shoulder without enclosing the upper arm
trap: On your raised knee while leaving the opposing elbow unrestrained

flashcards.question: Carni attack: what should be held before adding shoulder pressure?
flashcards.answer: Hold the wrist and elbow at a comfortable angle; a small change can load the shoulder rapidly.
flashcards.answer_line: The wrist and elbow at a controlled angle

plausible: The wrist alone with the elbow freely escaping
The triceps alone while the hand rotates freely
trap: The head alone with both of their arms loose

flashcards.question: Carni attack: how do you permit a tapped partner to unwind safely?
flashcards.answer: Release the wrist and leg clamp immediately on a tap or when the partner needs to roll safely.
flashcards.answer_line: Release the wrist and open the leg clamp

plausible: Release only the head frame while holding the wrist
Let the triceps go but keep the foot anchoring the shoulder
trap: Keep the clamp and ask them to roll through it

flashcards.question: Carni attack: which upper-body attachment accompanies the high guard leg at entry?
flashcards.answer: The guard player has a high leg and an overhook-side shoulder connection.

plausible: An underhook lifting the arm away from your high leg
A wrist-only pull with their elbow free between the bodies
trap: A two-handed head tie with neither upper arm enclosed

flashcards.answer: Richie Martinez demonstrates the configuration from Z guard through Jersey. The legs help anchor the upper body, but the submission target is the shoulder; a calf slicer, heel hook, or kneebar requires a separate lower-body capture.
flashcards.answer_line: A separately controlled bent leg and compression fulcrum

plausible: More pressure on the wrist already trapped in Carni
A tighter triceps grip without changing position
trap: A further belly-down turn around the captured shoulder
